title: Show HN: Run Google DataProc cluster on your local
author: jaysen_apache
raw_text:
Google does not provide official docker image for developers or AI agents to run dataproc cluster locally. so everybody need to spin up for even dev/CI testing,etc..now you or your AI agent can: 
docker run --rm agentcloud/dataproc:3.0.0-debian13 self-testsaves time and cost.it basically packages the same component version and make the hadoop and spark to developer.Here are docker images for other dataproc versions:https://hub.docker.com/r/agentcloud/dataproc/tagshere is full blog for more use-cases: https://local.cloud/blog/run-dataproc-locally-docker/
summary: This item introduces a docker image that lets you run a Google DataProc cluster locally on your machine. DataProc is Google Cloud's managed service for big data processing, primarily using Apache Hadoop and Spark. Traditionally, developing and testing applications for DataProc required spinning up a cloud cluster, which could be slow and costly for iterative development. This local solution provides a convenient way to simulate the DataProc environment, allowing you to develop, test, and debug your Spark and Hadoop jobs without cloud dependencies. It helps save time and money during the development and continuous integration phases. You could try pulling the docker image and running a basic spark word count example to see it in action.
why: Test big data pipelines locally, saving time and cloud costs.

title: Additional LLM SDK adapters beyond LangChain (OpenAI, GHCP) (theagentplane/tokenops)
raw_text:
Additional LLM SDK adapters beyond LangChain (OpenAI, GHCP) — open-source issue in theagentplane/tokenops. Labels: enhancement, help wanted, hacktoberfest. ## Summary

LangChain adapter work largely lands §12 for one platform, but `wrap_complete` still assumes a TokenOps-shaped `complete(...)` for other stacks. Real apps use raw OpenAI clients, GitHub Copilot (GHCP) SDK, and other model nodes — Brief’s ad-hoc bridges are not a general story.

**Area:** `wrap_complete`, provider adapters, field guide

## Desired behavior

- Thin **adapter interface**: normalize messages in/out + usage; plug into one governance wrap.
- Official adapters (or recipes)
summary:
This open-source issue highlights the need for more direct ways to connect with large language models (LLMs) from providers like OpenAI or GitHub Copilot, beyond relying solely on frameworks like LangChain. It suggests that many real-world applications interact with these LLMs using their native software development kits (SDKs). The current system might be too rigid, expecting a specific internal structure, and needs more flexible adapters to accommodate these direct SDK integrations. Understanding this distinction is crucial because while frameworks simplify development, direct SDK interaction offers more control and can be necessary for specific performance or customization needs.

One thing you could try is building a small application that calls the OpenAI API directly using its official Python client, rather than through LangChain. This will give you a clearer picture of how these underlying services work.
why: Direct LLM SDKs offer flexibility beyond frameworks, crucial for custom solutions.
